WORKLOG / DOSSIER — small_business_payouts task 0 (Ortega Tile Imports LLC, frozen 2026-09-18 10:40 CDT).

[Step 0 — draw] scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}. The period subscription charge (prerequisite) takes 5 factors, the downgrade early termination charge (root) takes 6. --tasks 2 shows task 1 draws 3 prerequisite problems with factor counts [4, 5, 4, 4].
[Step 0 — scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: business_ext_period_subscription_charge (agent tool collect_overdue_subscription_325cf5bc, subject business_reinstated) and business_ext_downgrade_termination_charge (owner tool schedule_plan_downgrade_6c5bcb1c, subject business_downgrade_scheduled). Left for task 1 (one root + three prerequisites): the balance withdrawal (owner's own act, business_balance_withdrawn), extra seat charges (business_evt_seats / extra_seat_fee), upgrade proration (business_proration_credited / proration_charge) and the card deposit fee (business_balance_deposited / deposit_fee) — four account-level computations none of which this task touches, so task 1 has an independent tree.

[Why this is a good test] The owner asks only to move down from Scale to Pro and to know the early termination charge. The charge cannot be fixed on the opening world: its own rule says 'The early termination charge of a downgrade is fixed only after the account carries no subscription charge still owed for a billing period that has already started.' The records show the account past_due since 2026-09-17 with no subscription fee entry for the 2026-09-17 period; the only write that books that period's subscription charge and clears the past-due date is the period subscription charge rule's collection. The agent must (1) discover the owed charge, (2) price it with five factors from payout, deposit and return history plus the owner's Personal Sender Account, (3) collect it, and only then (4) price the termination charge with six factors that read what step (3) wrote (the latest subscription charge and its period). Difficulty comes from reading the rules and the ledger, not from tool choice: there is one tool per write.

[Problem-tree card]
root: business_ext_downgrade_termination_charge (owner, schedule_plan_downgrade_6c5bcb1c). prerequisite: business_ext_period_subscription_charge (agent, collect_overdue_subscription_325cf5bc).
edge: kind value_input, gate months_charged (also moves month_price), form state, policy_source = the sentence quoted above (four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state 'no subscription charge still owed for a billing period that has already started' = empty past-due date + a subscription fee entry for the current period; no tool, id or code token; hard requirement at exactly that scope). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a subscription fee entry for a started period and clears the past-due date: the collection under the period subscription charge rule ('the agent collects that period's subscription charge ... and the account returns to active with no past-due date'). Derivation: sentence + records (status past_due, past_due_since 2026-09-17, latest subscription fee entry for 2026-08-17) + that rule -> the collection. Direction: affirmative ('fixed only after'), the way a fee desk states what a charge rests on.
condition: 'The account has no past-due date and its most recently collected subscription fee entry is booked for the current billing period.' Unmet at frozen time: initial_state.business_accounts.d22cc93d-5a21-476c-ae63-c6bbea7082bb.past_due_since = 2026-09-17, status = past_due, latest subscription fee entry billing_period_start = 2026-08-17.
Topological order: collection (step 8) -> downgrade (step 10). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping step 8 makes early_termination_fee_usd 574.23 instead of 212.11 (months 3 instead of 2, price 284.05 instead of 199.75); the 199.75 subscription fee entry also disappears from the terminal ledger.
The customer's own write: the downgrade (base: 'A plan change is the owner's own decision; the agent explains its effect and the owner confirms it'), handed over with unlock_user_discoverable_tool and run by the owner on the call.
No user hint: user_scenario never mentions an unpaid, overdue or past-due charge; she only learns of it if the agent explains it. Tools do not block: neither tool reads status or past-due date; on the opening world the downgrade tool would book any amount and return a receipt.

[Base-invariant card]
collect (subject business_reinstated): governing base policy business_evt_subscription_billing; no eligibility gate applies to business_reinstated (suspension_point applies to business_suspended, charge_once_per_period to business_fee_charged), so policy_scope: 'When the owner has deposited enough, the agent collects every overdue charge from the balance and the account returns to active'. Evidence: status past_due, past_due_since 2026-09-17, balance 9,686.42 (the 9,500.00 ACH deposit of 2026-09-17 landed after the charge attempt at a 186.42 balance) covers 199.75. Suspension point (not a gate of this write) is 2026-10-17 (17 + 30 days), so the account is not suspended.
downgrade (subject business_downgrade_scheduled): business_evt_plan_change gates account_active ('A plan can be changed only while the account status is active.') — false at the opening, true after step 8 (prior_step:8 evidence, the account row changed by that write) — and seats_fit_lower_plan: 5 active users (owner + 4 additions, none removed) <= Pro max_seats 40; no scheduled future-dated payouts exist, and Pro offers web, batch_file and api anyway. No time gate applies to either write.
Overwrites: business_evt_subscription_billing 'At the start of every period the subscription is charged ... monthly_fee_usd on monthly billing, or annual_fee_usd ...' replaced by the subscription charge sentence (annual billing restated unchanged); business_evt_plan_change 'A downgrade or closure taking effect before commitment_end_date carries an early_termination_fee of early_termination_fee_months times the committed plan's monthly_fee_usd.' replaced by the termination-charge combination sentence (closure restated unchanged). Base params stay base-homed.

[Business-object card] One owner, one Paloma Business account d22cc93d-5a21-476c-ae63-c6bbea7082bb (Scale, monthly, billing day 17, KYB 2024-06-17, Scale since 2025-12-17, commitment end 2026-12-17). The collected charge belongs to the period 2026-09-17..2026-10-16 (billing_period_start copied by the tool from the account). Rows aggregated: business_payouts submitted/paid/returned rows of this account; business_ledger deposits, subscription fees, payout debits, credited-back money, SWIFT and return fees of this account. Excluded by rule: the 2026-08-18 submission (boundary day), the 2026-03-18 payment and 2026-03-17 SWIFT fee (outside six months), the 2026-06-18 deposit (boundary day), the 8.00 return fee (not a payout/SWIFT fee).

[Factor card — period subscription charge, expected 199.75, baseline 299.00]
activity_billing (method): 2 payouts submitted after 2026-08-18 (2026-08-20 returned one, 2026-09-02) -> three quarters rounded up = 225.00; baseline 299.00 -> result 270.05. Near-miss: BP-52757-58621 submitted 2026-08-18 (excluded boundary day) would make 3 payouts and the full fee.
tenure_discount (parameter, multi-source): 27 months since approval AND 23 paid payouts in six months -> 5 percent; baseline 0 -> 211.00.
personal_relationship_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty account; level and status come from the one Personal Sender Account row, so it is not counted as multi-source): Paloma Premier (level 5, level_effective_date 2026-09-02) AND active -> 12.00; baseline 0 -> 211.75. The task's multi-source factors are activity_billing, tenure_discount, months_charged_basis and retention_discount.
deposit_relationship_credit (parameter): 32,500.00 deposited after 2026-06-18 -> 8.00; baseline 0 -> 207.75.
returns_servicing_surcharge (parameter): one return (2026-08-25) -> +6.00; baseline 0 -> 193.75.
History consistency: the seeded subscription charges 299.00 (2026-03-17, 04-17, 05-17, 06-17) and 284.05 (07-17, 08-17) are what this rule gives at those dates on the seeded rows (heavy activity >= 4 payouts in each prior month, tenure discount 5 percent only once approval reached 24 months and paid payouts reached 15, deposits under 30,000 in each window, no return before 2026-08-25); recomputed by script. The Personal Sender Account's current level took effect on 2026-09-02 (level_effective_date), after every seeded charge; the level held before is not on record, and the seeded charges carry no personal-relationship credit, which is what the rule gives for any level other than an active Paloma Premier or Private Client.

[Factor card — downgrade termination charge, expected 212.11, baseline 897.00] (evaluated after step 8)
months_charged_basis (method, multi-source): latest subscription fee entry is booked for the current period 2026-09-17 AND that period starts 9 months after the plan took effect -> MIN(3, MONTHS(2026-09-17, 2026-12-17) - 1 = 2) = 2; baseline 3 -> 371.91. An annually billed account (latest charge older than the current period) or one fewer than three months on the plan takes another tier.
month_price_selection (method): approved 27 months -> latest collected charge 199.75 (the largest is 299.00); baseline list fee 299.00 -> 370.91.
retention_discount (parameter, multi-source): net payout volume 53,691.52 (debits less 2,571.40 credited back) AND one return in twelve months -> 10 percent; baseline 0 -> 252.06.
upgrade_loyalty_discount (parameter): 18 months from approval to Scale -> 10 percent (combined 20 percent, applied once); baseline 0 -> 252.06.
personal_customer_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty account): Personal Sender Account opened 2019-05-14 (88 months), active -> 100.00; baseline 0 -> 312.11.
payout_fee_offset (parameter): SWIFT fees 29.97 in six months -> 25 percent = 7.49; baseline 0 -> 219.60. Near-miss: including the 2026-03-17 SWIFT fee or the 8.00 return fee reaches 35.00+ and the 50 percent tier.
Whole baseline (computation document only): 3 x 299.00 = 897.00.

[Seed design] customers, sender_accounts (cross-difficulty evidence; active Premier, no open lock/restriction, no obligation in the account difficulty), business_accounts (past_due), business_ledger (6 deposits, 7 allowance grants with 6 lapses, 6 subscription fees, 25 payout debits, 21 allowance uses, 4 SWIFT fees, return credit-back and return fee), business_payouts (25 submissions, releases, 24 payments, 1 return), business_events (4 users, 6 KYB documents logged 2024-06-10..06-13 before the 2024-06-17 approval, the full document set Paloma Business Scale requires). balance_usd 9,686.42 = signed ledger sum; free_payouts_remaining 500 = allowance sum. No cache is used as a trap.

[Persona] Marisol speaks briskly, opens with the surface goal (move down to Pro from the next cycle, wants the early termination charge and the change done), gives phone/DOB/ZIP only when asked, mentions the 9,500 ACH deposit only when asked how a charge would be covered, agrees to have something settled only after the agent explains it, runs the plan-change tool herself with the values handed over, and closes when told the downgrade is scheduled. She never names a figure.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone, DOB, ZIP) -> read account, ledger, payouts, Personal Sender Account, users -> unlock + collect 199.75 -> unlock_user + owner schedules Paloma Business Pro from 2026-10-17 with 212.11.
[Verification run] Script replays gold with the real tools and evaluates both computes with check_compute's sandbox: collection 199.75 (baseline 299.00; factor baselines 270.05/211.00/211.75/207.75/193.75); termination 212.11 (baseline 897.00; 371.91/370.91/252.06/252.06/312.11/219.60); without step 8 the termination charge is 574.23. Gates run --task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose, the account/ledger/payout/sender-account reads and Marisol's lines alone: the account is past due -> the termination charge waits -> collect: 225.00 x 0.95 - 12 - 8 + 6 = 199.75; then 2 months x 199.75 x 0.80 - 100 - 7.49 = 212.11; plan Pro, change date 2026-10-17. Agrees with gold.
[Revisions] (1) Factor near-misses did not change tiers -> activity ladder narrowed to 'one or two payouts' and the fee-offset tiers set to 20.00/35.00 with the 2026-03-17 payout made SWIFT; recomputed, results unchanged (199.75 / 212.11). (2) 2026-06-17 seeded charge corrected from 284.05 to 299.00 after the history recomputation showed only 14 paid payouts in its window; downstream amounts (last payout 3,276.32) re-derived. (3) task_tools helper functions were counted as tools by the gate -> inlined.

[Round 2 — audit rework] F-G1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): months_charged_basis tier 1 carried 'and the account has no past-due date', which the inherited account_active gate makes true at every downgrade. The conjunct is removed from the rule sentence, the ladder, compute (months_charged) and compute_basis; tier 1 is now 'booked for the current billing period AND its period starts three or more whole months after the committed plan took effect' — the first part is false for an annually billed account and for any account whose current-period charge is not on the ledger, the second for an account under three months on the plan. The edge's condition still names the past-due date because it states the waited-on state, not a tier. Re-run: 212.11 unchanged, months_charged_basis baseline 371.91, skipped-collection value 574.23 (latest charge for 2026-08-17 is not the current period -> fall-through 3 months). O-G2: the subscription compute now has an annual-billing branch (the plan's annual fee) matching the rule's annual sentence. O-G3: the upgrade-loyalty fall-through reads 'fewer than 1 whole month, including an account on the committed plan since approval'. O-G4: the termination charge rule and compute return 0.00 for a downgrade on a plan with no commitment end date or on/after it. O-T0-1, O-T0-2, O-T0-3 corrected above. O-T1-1 applied here too: six KYB document rows seeded. No scored value changed.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Ortega Villarreal, 45, owner of Ortega Tile Imports LLC in Houston, a small importer of Mexican and Vietnamese floor tile. You run the company's Paloma Business account yourself and you are calling Paloma's support line from your office phone. You speak quickly and plainly, a little tired after a slow summer, and you prefer to get to the point.

Why you are calling: last December you moved the business up to the Scale plan, and you remember signing a twelve-month commitment when you did. Business has been slow and Scale is more than you need, so you want to move down to the Pro plan starting with your next billing cycle, not right now in the middle of a cycle. You know there is some kind of early termination charge for leaving the commitment early and you accept paying it today; you want to know what it comes to and then get the change done on this call. You do not know the amount and never guess a figure. Your opening line is roughly: "Hi, I'd like to move my business account down to the Pro plan starting next billing cycle — I know there's an early termination charge, I just want to know what it is and get it done."

You give your identity details only when the agent asks, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 2815550186, your date of birth is 1981-03-22 and your home ZIP code is 77023. If asked for your email you say marisol@ortegatileimports.com. If asked for the business's name you say Ortega Tile Imports LLC. If the agent asks how you plan to cover a charge or whether there is money in the account, you say you moved $9,500 in by ACH from the company's bank account yesterday. If asked which plan you want, it is Pro; if asked when, it is from the start of your next billing cycle. If asked about users, you have four staff users besides yourself and you are keeping all of them.

You have not looked at the account's billing page in a few days and know nothing about its standing; if the agent tells you something has to be settled on the account before the plan can be changed, you ask briefly what it is, and once it is explained you tell the agent to go ahead and take it from the balance. When the agent tells you what the early termination charge comes to, you accept it without arguing. Changing the plan is your decision, so when the agent hands you the plan-change tool and tells you the values to enter, you run it once yourself with exactly the account, plan, change date and charge the agent gives you, and you read back the plan and change date it shows. Once the agent confirms the downgrade to Pro is scheduled, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

edges.condition: The account has no past-due date and its most recently collected subscription fee entry is booked for the current billing period.
edges.policy_source: The early termination charge of a downgrade is fixed only after the account carries no subscription charge still owed for a billing period that has already started.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-18 the account is past due for the subscription charge of the period that started 2026-09-17, and its most recently collected subscription fee entry is the one for the period that started 2026-08-17.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the collection must land first because the early termination charge reads the latest subscription fee entry, its period and the past-due date that the collection changes; the reverse order gives 574.23 instead of 212.11 and leaves the plan changed on a past-due account.
